# Generated by rules/link.sh. Do not edit this file.

Edit files in `rules/` and run `rules/link.sh`.

# Communication

- Do not use em dash or en dash characters.
- Write user-facing text in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
- Start status reports with the result, then give the evidence.

# Git and GitHub

- Use conventional commits.
- Never force push.
- Do not use a bare `#N` in a GitHub comment or pull request body. Write
  `item 1`, `(2)`, or a plain list. Use `#NNNN` only for a real pull request or
  issue.
- Work happens in a git worktree on a short-lived branch.
- Before a branch lands, `pnpm verify` and the relevant browser tests must
  pass.
- To land a branch, rebase it onto `main`, fast-forward merge it, then delete
  it. Pull requests are not required.
- Stay inside the active worktree. All edits, commits, and untracked files
  belong in that worktree.

# Product design

- Use Tailwind CSS utilities for application layout and presentation.
- Do not add handwritten CSS selectors, CSS modules, component style sheets,
  or inline `style` properties.
- `apps/web/src/tailwind.css` is the only application CSS source. It can have
  only Tailwind imports, source registration, and central theme variables.
- Keep color, typography, spacing, radius, and shadow decisions in the central
  Tailwind theme and runtime palette. Do not add arbitrary Tailwind values.
- Use the named type scale. Body text is 14 px. Control text is 13 px. Use the
  standard Tailwind heading scale. Do not add one-off font sizes.
- Use the standard Tailwind spacing scale. Do not add one-off pixel or rem
  spacing values.
- A typed adapter for a third-party rendering system, such as CodeMirror, can
  set presentation in TypeScript only when utility classes cannot reach its
  generated DOM. It must use the central Tailwind and semantic theme variables.
- Use native semantic elements. Every icon-only action must have an accessible
  name and a title when the purpose is not clear from context.
- Keep keyboard focus visible. Dialogs must support Escape. Important actions
  must be possible without a pointer.
- Use compact controls by default. Keep controls large enough for reliable
  pointer and touch input.

# Application architecture

- Keep package boundaries strict. Domain code must not import transport,
  database, browser, or React code.
- Use generated API client operations. Do not write request URLs or direct
  `fetch` calls in feature code.
- Treat browser drafts as recovery data, not server versions. Only an explicit
  Save action creates an immutable server version.
- Keep one CodeMirror editor instance for an open working copy. Do not replace
  its document during a React render, theme change, or preview update.
- Store note paths with one `.md` suffix. Hide this storage detail from the
  person who edits the note name.
- Keep rich Markdown rendering isolated from network and storage access. Pass
  attachments and diagram rendering through typed resolvers.
- Validate at domain boundaries. Do not weaken a server invariant to hide a
  client defect.

# Verification

- Add a regression test for each fixed defect.
- Cover every P0 user journey with a browser test that uses the public
  interface and checks the server result.
- A first-user test must start with an empty database and must use the real
  setup screen. Do not create its account through a test-only bootstrap route.
- Run focused tests while work is in progress. Run `pnpm verify` before a
  change is ready to merge.
- Run the browser matrix when navigation, persistence, keyboard behavior, or
  editor rendering changes.
- Do not weaken assertions, add fixed delays, or skip a failing test to make a
  suite pass.
